title: Common Traps and How to Avoid Them
tagline: Year 4 — Twenty classic aptitude traps: successive percentages, average speed, wrong bases, counting errors and unit slips

introduction.overview: Most lost marks come from a small set of traps rather than from hard mathematics. In each trap there is a tempting answer reached by an intuitive but wrong step, and a correct answer reached by one extra check. Setters place the tempting answer among the options. This chapter lists the traps with the wrong step, the correct step and a quick test for each: successive percentages that add, averages of speeds, the wrong base for a percentage, inclusive counting, fence-post counting, unit slips, mixtures with replacement, and compounding periods.
introduction.placementRelevance: Knowing the traps lets you spot a tempting option and pause for ten seconds.
introduction.realWorldContext: Common-error awareness is the basis of quality checks in any field.

learningObjectives: Recognise the trap behind a tempting option
Apply the one extra check that avoids it
Use the correct base for percentages
Count inclusively and at boundaries correctly

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A tempting option is usually the answer of the intuitive but wrong step.

coreDefinitions: Trap: an error that many make for the same reason.
Tempting option: the wrong answer from the trap.
Base error: using the wrong quantity for a percentage.
Boundary error: miscounting at the ends.
Check: the extra step that catches the trap.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: If an answer comes too easily, ask what trap might be hiding.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Ask: is there a base, a boundary or a unit I could have mishandled?

mainNarrative: Successive discounts of 20% and 10% on ₹1,000: 1,000 × 0.8 × 0.9 = ₹720, not ₹700.
Average speed for equal distances at 60 and 40 km/h is 48, not 50.
If B is 20% more than A, then A is 20 ÷ 120 = 16.7% less than B, not 20%.
Posts every 2 m along 10 m make 10 ÷ 2 + 1 = 6 posts.

deepDiveAspects.title: Compounding periods
deepDiveAspects.content: Half-yearly compounding at 10% per annum is 5% twice: 1.05² = 1.1025.

solvedExamples.title: Successive
solvedExamples.question: Discounts of 20% and 10% on ₹1,000. Final price?

solvedExamples.title: Reverse percent
solvedExamples.question: B is 20% more than A. A is what percent less than B?

solvedExamples.title: Fence posts
solvedExamples.question: Posts every 2 m along a 10 m fence, including both ends. How many posts?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: When the answer comes too easily, check base, boundary and unit before choosing.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The tempting option is often adjacent to the right one.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Keep a personal trap list from mocks.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Ten seconds of checking saves a mark.
